title: Transport of coherent formal modules along a scheme isomorphism
statement: Let $X,Y$ be Noetherian schemes, let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf, and let $e:X\cong Y$ be a scheme isomorphism. With coherent formal modules as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], there exists an equivalence $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)\simeq\mathit{Coh}(Y,(e^{-1})^*\mathcal I)$, where the transported ideal is the comap along $e^{-1}$. No abelian structure on either formal category is assumed.

source.place: Section 0EHN, definition of coherent formal modules; Lemma 087W affine presentation and Lemma 0887 pullback of formal systems, specialized to inverse scheme isomorphisms

proof.text: Apply the formal-system pullback construction to e inverse and to e. Its equations with the full-subcategory inclusions specify the termwise module pullbacks and their maps, and give functors between the two formal categories.

source.place: Section 0EHN, definition of coherent formal modules; Lemma 087W affine presentation and Lemma 0887 pullback of formal systems, specialized to inverse scheme isomorphisms

proof.text: Comap of ideals along the inverse composites is the original ideal. The pullback composition and identity isomorphisms yield natural isomorphisms between the two composites of the functors and the identity functors. Invariance of the three formal object conditions under natural isomorphism permits restricting these isomorphisms to the full subcategories.

source.place: Section 0EHN, definition of coherent formal modules; Lemma 087W affine presentation and Lemma 0887 pullback of formal systems, specialized to inverse scheme isomorphisms

proof.text: The restricted functors and the two natural isomorphisms define the equivalence, by Equivalence.mk. This is equivalence data for inverse scheme isomorphisms, not a use of abelianness or of the coimage-image conclusion.
